subject: Pilot pricing: publishable ratecard vs surge pool
messages:
From: Ethan Brooks <ethan@vertexhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vertex Health Procurement <procurement@vertexhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing and runout — options for short extension

Karthik,

Quick follow up from this morning's engineering sync — we are close on the integration but hit a burn-rate spike in the last week. We have about two weeks of runway left under the current pilot plan.

Our procurement lead asked whether you can either: 1) provide a publishable pilot ratecard with a short-term discount we can include in the PO, or 2) offer a surge pool we can top up immediately (one-time token bucket) with a clear invoice so we can avoid an amendment.

Ballpark budget from my side: up to $25k for an immediate bridge to get us through testing. Important: procurement wants a line item (rate) they can commit to in a PO if we go the ratecard route.

Can you outline two concrete options (timeboxed extension + PO-ready rates vs surge credits)? Also let me know any lead-time for legal/finance review.

Thanks — Ethan
Ethan Brooks
Director, Applied ML
Vertex Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing and runout — options for short extension

Ethan — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the progress. Short answer: yes, we can do both. High-level options below, I'll attach a short proposal after we align internally.

Option A — Publishable pilot ratecard (PO-ready):
- 30-day pilot extension
- Publishable ratecard lines: generation tokens and embedding units
- Pilot discount: 20% off standard list for the pilot period if PO is received within 7 days
- Outcome: PO references the rate lines; billing via standard invoice

Option B — Surge pool (one-time token top-up):
- Immediate start: one-time token bucket (recommended for rapid ramp)
- Example: 200k-generation-token pool
- Discount: 35% off list on surge pool credit price for one-time purchase
- Outcome: simple invoice, no PO amendment needed for the original pilot addendum

Ask: Which price model do you prefer? If you want Option A, procurement's requirement for a publishable line is fine — we can surface that in the proposal PDF. If Option B, we can draft an invoice and a short SOW for bookkeeping.

Attaching a working draft of the proposal (redwood-pilot-proposal-v2.pdf) with sample numbers. I copied Priyom to confirm finance/tier approvals.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 20:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot pricing and runout — internal pricing check

Karthik / Kimberly — quick internal note after reviewing Karthik's draft:

- Finance view: 20% pilot discount is standard and OK without exec approval for deals under $30k. Anything north of 25% needs manager sign-off.
- Surge pool: 35% off on a one-time small token bundle is doable as a promotional cap, but we should limit to a single-month bridge.
- Legal: ratecard PO will require our standard pilot T&Cs; I recommend attaching the redwood-ratecard-terms.pdf and mark the PO clause for net-30 invoicing.

Next steps for internal: Karthik, if you aim to offer the 35% surge, I can OK operationally today. If you go for the publishable ratecard + 20% discount and they want the discount written into the PO, we should route to Kimberly for final pricing sign-off before sending the DocuSign.

Priyom
Priyom Das
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan@vertexhealth.com>, Vertex Health Procurement <procurement@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing — final options and doc links

Ethan / Procurement team — following up with two firm paths so you can choose and move forward quickly. Attaching the ratecard terms for PO (redwood-ratecard-terms.pdf) and the short proposal (redwood-pilot-proposal-v2.pdf).

Path 1 — Publishable ratecard (PO route)
- 30-day extension, publishable per-line rates for generation and embeddings
- Pilot discount: 20% off list for the pilot period; must be captured in the PO (we will include rate lines and a discount note)
- Billing: net-30 invoice after pilot period or pro-rata on signature
- Advantage: clean PO and predictable unit economics if you want to roll forward

Path 2 — Surge pool (fast bridge)
- Immediate one-time purchase of a token bucket: 200,000 generation tokens
- Discount: 35% off the surge-credit list price for this one-time purchase
- Billing: one-time invoice; no PO amendment required to continue integration
- Advantage: instant capacity, lowest friction for engineering to continue testing

Callout: Per internal guidance, I can approve the 35% surge discount as an operational promotion for a one-month bridge. For the publishable ratecard discount to be >25% we'd need Kimberly's sign-off, but 20% is fully within the standard playbook.

Next steps:
- If you want the surge pool, reply with the billing contact and we will issue an invoice within 4 hours.
- If you want the ratecard PO, reply with the PO number and we will prepare the DocuSign packet (link below) and include the publishable lines in the PO-ready PDF.

DocuSign link (ratecard packet): https://www.docusign.com/packet/ABCD1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/83472

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Brooks <ethan@vertexhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vertex Health Procurement <procurement@vertexhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing — final options and doc links

Thanks — we’ll take the surge pool to move fast. Please issue the one-time invoice for the 200,000 token bundle at the 35% discount and send payment instructions; procurement will follow up with a PO for accounting (procurement@vertexhealth.com) to match the invoice.

Ethan
Ethan Brooks
Director, Applied ML
Vertex Health
